title: Transit Gateway Route Table Attachment Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `eventSource="ec2.amazonaws.com" (eventName="CreateTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="DeleteTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="ReplaceTransitGatewayRoute")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.72 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `eventSource="ec2.amazonaws.com" (eventName="CreateTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="DeleteTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="ReplaceTransitGatewayRoute")`. Confirm UC-4.1.72 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.

description: UC-4.1.72 — Transit Gateway Route Table Attachment Health: queries AWS `aws:cloudtrail` for `CreateTransitGatewayRoute`, `DeleteTransitGatewayRoute`, `ReplaceTransitGatewayRoute` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On AWS, unapproved creation tied to 'Transit Gateway Route Table Attachment Health' expands credential and network attack surface and often precedes persistence or crypto-mining activity. UC-4.1.72 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Alert on route changes in production TGW tables. Correlate with change windows. Combine with UC-4.1.58 metrics for end-to-end path validation. Use Network Manager events if enabled.
visualization: Timeline (route changes), Table (route table, CIDR, action), Line chart (cross-VPC bytes with UC-4.1.58).
cimSpl: | tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Change.All_Changes by All_Changes.user | sort - count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Alert on route changes in production TGW tables. Correlate with change windows. Combine with UC-4.1.58 metrics for end-to-end path validation. Use Network Manager events if enabled.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="ec2.amazonaws.com" (eventName="CreateTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="DeleteTransitGatewayRoute" OR eventName="ReplaceTransitGatewayRoute")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.72_transit_gateway_route_ta_72"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect transit gateway route table attachment health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_72_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Timeline (route changes), Table (route table, CIDR, action), Line chart (cross-VPC bytes with UC-4.1.58)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
